title: Common Punctuation
text: Hello, world! How are you? I'm fine, thank you. It's a beautiful day; the sun is shining. "What time is it?" she asked. He replied, "It's 3:30 PM." Wow! That's great.

title: Special Characters
text: @#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;':",./<>? Email: user@example.com Password: P@ssw0rd! Website: https://www.example.com Phone: (555) 123-4567

title: Brackets and Parentheses
text: Arrays [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] and objects {name: "John", age: 30} are common in programming. Mathematical expressions like (a + b) * (c - d) use parentheses for grouping.

title: Quotation Practice
text: "The best way to predict the future is to invent it," said Alan Kay. 'Single quotes' and "double quotes" are both used in writing. Programming languages use quotes: 'string' and "another string".

title: Semicolons and Colons
text: There are three things to remember: practice, patience, and persistence. JavaScript uses semicolons; they separate statements. Time format: 12:30 PM; Date format: 2024:01:15.

title: Dashes and Hyphens
text: Well-known facts include: mother-in-law, twenty-one, self-confident. Em dashes—like this one—separate clauses. En dashes (1990–2000) show ranges. Hyphens connect compound words.

title: Mixed Punctuation
text: Dr. Smith said, "The patient's temperature is 98.6°F." The meeting is scheduled for 2:30 PM; however, it might be delayed. Please review items #1, #2, and #3 before Friday's deadline.
